name: Frank Shu
milestone_by_age_26: Completed PhD at Harvard in 1968 (age 25) proposing the density wave theory of spiral galaxy structure with C.C. Lin, and began assistant professorship at SUNY Stony Brook the same year.
early_history_summary: Born in Kunming, China to a mathematics professor father, Shu emigrated to the US at age 5 and enrolled at MIT at 16. He worked under applied mathematician C.C. Lin on spiral density-wave theory as an undergraduate, then continued with Lin as his graduate advisor at Harvard, publishing the foundational density wave theory papers during his PhD studies.
family_context_summary: Son of Shien-siu Shu, a mathematics professor who later became president of National Tsing Hua University; family emigrated from China to the US when Shu was 5, settling in the Midwest.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a mathematics professor at Illinois Institute of Technology, providing an academic household environment and connection to mentor C.C. Lin who refocused the young Shu on astrophysics.
evidence_summary: Frank Shu was born to an academic family in China and emigrated to the US at age 5. His father, a mathematics professor, connected him to C.C. Lin at MIT, who became his mentor and guided him toward astrophysics. Shu enrolled at MIT at 16 and completed his BS in physics at 20, then pursued a PhD at Harvard under Lin's continued guidance. By age 25, he had co-developed the density wave theory of spiral galaxies and began an assistant professorship at Stony Brook, marking a major intellectual achievement before 26.
starting_point: Born in Kunming, China in 1943 to an academic family; father was a mathematics professor who emigrated to the US when Shu was an infant, and the family reunited in the American Midwest when Shu was 5.
current_position: Died on April 22, 2023 at age 79 in Atherton, California; final roles included Distinguished Professor at UC San Diego and University Professor emeritus across UC campuses, and former president of National Tsing Hua University (2002-2006).

trajectory.event: Completed BS in physics at MIT, having worked on spiral galaxy structure under C.C. Lin.
Earned PhD from Harvard University and co-developed the density wave theory of spiral galaxies with C.C. Lin; began assistant professorship at SUNY Stony Brook.
Promoted to Full Professor at UC Berkeley.
Became Chairman of the Astronomy Department at UC Berkeley.
Awarded the title of University Professor across all UC campuses.
Became President of National Tsing Hua University in Taiwan, a position his father had held three decades earlier.
Joined Academia Sinica's Institute of Astronomy and Astrophysics as Distinguished Research Fellow.
Died on April 22, 2023 in Atherton, California.

name: João Gilberto
milestone_by_age_26: By age 19 (1950), Gilberto was a professional radio performer in Rio de Janeiro as a member of the vocal group Garotos da Lua on Radio Tupi, establishing himself in Brazil's music industry.
early_history_summary: Born in Juazeiro, Bahia to a wealthy merchant father, Gilberto received his first guitar from his grandfather at age 14 and was leading a band within a year. At 18 he moved to Salvador to perform on live radio, then joined Garotos da Lua and relocated to Rio de Janeiro, performing regularly on Radio Tupi by around 1950.
family_context_summary: Son of a wealthy merchant in Juazeiro, Bahia; father insisted on education for all seven children but disapproved of music as a career. Grandfather bought him his first guitar at age 14.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a wealthy merchant with no musical background; grandfather supported the musical interest by gifting the first guitar despite the father's disapproval.
evidence_summary: João Gilberto was born to a wealthy merchant family in Bahia, Brazil. His grandfather bought him a guitar at 14 against his father's wishes, and within a year he was leading a school band. By 18 he was performing on live radio in Salvador, and by approximately 1950 he had joined Garotos da Lua and moved to Rio de Janeiro to perform on Radio Tupi, making him a professional musician in Brazil's largest media market before age 20. His obsessive, solitary practice sessions later produced the signature bossa nova style that would define a genre.
starting_point: Born in 1931 in Juazeiro, Bahia, Brazil to a wealthy merchant father who insisted on education for all seven children; grandfather gifted him his first guitar at age 14.
current_position: Died on July 6, 2019 at age 88 in Rio de Janeiro; final status was as a reclusive living legend of bossa nova, widely regarded as the 'father of bossa nova.'

trajectory.event: Joined vocal group Garotos da Lua and performed regularly on Radio Tupi in Rio de Janeiro as a professional musician.
Recorded his first bossa nova singles including 'Chega de Saudade,' which launched the bossa nova genre.
Released debut album 'Chega de Saudade,' cementing bossa nova as a major musical movement.
The album Getz/Gilberto with Stan Getz won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year, the first jazz record to do so.
Won the Grammy Award for Best World Music Album for 'João voz e violão.'
Died on July 6, 2019 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

name: Anderson Silva
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Shooto Middleweight Championship on August 26, 2001 (age 26) by defeating previously undefeated Hayato Sakurai, becoming the first man to defeat Sakurai in his first 20 fights.
early_history_summary: Born into poverty in São Paulo and raised by his aunt and uncle in Curitiba, Silva began training jiu-jitsu with neighborhood kids as a child, then took up taekwondo, capoeira, and muay thai as a teenager. He made his professional MMA debut in 1997 at age 22 and compiled an 8-1 record before winning the Shooto title in 2001.
family_context_summary: Born into a poverty-stricken family in São Paulo; raised by his aunt and uncle in Curitiba, with his uncle being a police officer. No documented family resources for athletic training.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family domain advantage documented; uncle was a police officer but no martial arts background noted in family.
evidence_summary: Anderson Silva was born into poverty in São Paulo and raised by relatives in Curitiba, where he began training in multiple martial arts disciplines as a child and teenager. He made his professional MMA debut in 1997 at age 22 and by 2001 had compiled an 8-1 record. At age 26, he defeated the undefeated Hayato Sakurai to win the Shooto Middleweight Championship, a major international title. His early training at the renowned Chute Boxe Academy in Curitiba, a hub for MMA talent, provided critical infrastructure despite his lack of family resources.
starting_point: Born in 1975 in São Paulo, Brazil into a poverty-stricken family; raised by his aunt and uncle (a police officer) in Curitiba from age 4.
current_position: Retired from MMA and boxing; inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame in July 2023; widely regarded as one of the greatest mixed martial artists of all time with a record 16-fight UFC win streak and 2,457-day title reign.

trajectory.event: Made professional MMA debut in Brazil with a pair of wins.
Won the Shooto Middleweight Championship by defeating previously undefeated Hayato Sakurai in Japan.
Debuted in the UFC and won the UFC Middleweight Championship by defeating Rich Franklin.
Set the UFC record for longest title reign at 2,457 days with 16 consecutive victories and 10 title defenses.
Left the UFC and transitioned to professional boxing, defeating Julio Cesar Chavez Jr.
Inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame in July 2023.

name: Eduard Azaryan
milestone_by_age_26: Won USSR championship in team all-around and earned silver at the 1978 World Artistic Gymnastics Championships at age 20, then Olympic gold in team all-around at the 1980 Moscow Olympics at age 22.
early_history_summary: Son of three-time Olympic champion Albert Azaryan, Eduard began gymnastics at age 7 under his father's direct coaching at a children's gymnastics school in Yerevan. By 1978 he had joined the USSR national gymnastics team, winning national and international medals, culminating in Olympic gold in 1980.
family_context_summary: Son of Albert Azaryan, one of the greatest gymnasts of the 1950s and three-time Olympic champion, who coached Eduard from age 7 at his children's gymnastics school in Yerevan.
evidence_summary: Eduard Azaryan was born into an extraordinary gymnastics family: his father Albert Azaryan was a three-time Olympic champion known as the 'King of Rings.' Albert began coaching Eduard at age 7 at his children's gymnastics school in Yerevan, making the gym 'his second home.' By 1978 at age 20, Eduard had joined the USSR national team, won the USSR championship, and earned silver at the World Championships. He won Olympic gold in the team all-around at the 1980 Moscow Olympics at age 22, all before turning 26.
starting_point: Born in 1958 in Yerevan, Armenia (Soviet Union) to Albert Azaryan, a three-time Olympic champion gymnast who coached him from age 7 at his own children's gymnastics school.
current_position: Emigrated to the USA in 1992; owns and operates Azarian Gymnastics in Aliso Viejo, California with his wife Marina.

trajectory.event: Became USSR champion in team all-around, won bronze at World Cup and silver at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships.
Won Olympic gold medal in the team all-around at the Moscow Summer Olympics.
Emigrated to the United States with his family.
Established Azarian Gymnastics training facility in Aliso Viejo, California.

name: Finn Tveter
milestone_by_age_26: Won a bronze medal at the 1970 World Rowing Championships in the coxed four at age 23, and competed at the 1972 Munich Olympics, establishing himself as an elite international rower before 26.
early_history_summary: A Norwegian rower from Norske Studenters Roklubb in Oslo, Tveter competed at the highest levels of international rowing in the early 1970s, winning World Championship bronze in 1970 and competing at two Olympic Games (1972 and 1976). He later became a jurist and director of the Norwegian Association of Real Estate Agents.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Skøyen and Bøler in Oslo, Norway; older brother influenced his competitive drive. Family background details not extensively documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Finn Tveter was a Norwegian rower from Oslo who competed for Norske Studenters Roklubb. By age 23 he had won a bronze medal at the 1970 World Rowing Championships in the coxed four, and by 26 he had also competed at the 1972 Munich Olympics. His physical stature (194 cm, 92 kg) and membership in Norway's premier rowing club provided the foundation for elite-level competition. He later became a jurist, serving as director of the Norwegian Association of Real Estate Agents for 17 years.
starting_point: Born in 1947 in Oslo, Norway; grew up in Skøyen and Bøler neighborhoods; family background not extensively documented.
current_position: Died on July 30, 2018 at age 70 in Oslo; final role was director of the Norwegian Association of Real Estate Agents (NEF) from 1997 to 2018, having previously served as a jurist and chairman of the Bankklagenemnda.

trajectory.event: Won bronze medal at the World Rowing Championships in the coxed four.
Competed at the Munich Summer Olympics.
Won Olympic silver medal in the coxless four at the Montreal Summer Olympics.
Became director of the Norwegian Association of Real Estate Agents (NEF).
Died on July 30, 2018 in Oslo, Norway.

name: Jerzy Skolimowski
milestone_by_age_26: Directed his feature debut 'Identification Marks: None' (Rysopis) in 1964 at age 26, which won awards at festivals in Arnhem and Warsaw; had previously co-written Andrzej Wajda's 'Innocent Sorcerers' (1960) and Roman Polanski's 'Knife in the Water' (1961).
early_history_summary: Born in Łódź to an architect father who was executed by the Nazis, Skolimowski grew up scarred by wartime experiences. He studied ethnography at Warsaw University, published poetry, boxed, and played drums in a jazz band before entering the Łódź Film School. His connections to the Polish film scene through jazz composer Krzysztof Komeda led to early screenwriting work with Wajda and Polanski.
family_context_summary: Son of an architect father who was executed by the Nazis for resistance activity, and a mother who hid a Jewish family during the war. Childhood was deeply scarred by World War II experiences in Warsaw.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an architect and member of the Polish Resistance, executed by Nazis; no direct film industry family background, but intellectual/artistic household environment.
evidence_summary: Jerzy Skolimowski was born in Łódź, Poland in 1938 to an architect father who was executed by the Nazis for resistance activity. His wartime childhood profoundly shaped his artistic vision. He studied ethnography at Warsaw University, where he was active in poetry, boxing, and jazz, connecting him to composer Krzysztof Komeda and through him to the Polish film scene. By his early twenties he had co-written major films with Andrzej Wajda and Roman Polański, and at 26 he directed his award-winning feature debut 'Identification Marks: None,' assembled from student films at the Łódź Film School.
starting_point: Born in 1938 in Łódź, Poland to an architect father (executed by Nazis for resistance activity) and a mother who hid a Jewish family during the war; childhood deeply scarred by World War II.
current_position: Living in Poland as an active filmmaker and painter; returned to filmmaking after a 17-year hiatus with 'Four Nights with Anna' (2008) and continues to direct, with 'EO' (2022) winning the Jury Prize at Cannes.

trajectory.event: Co-wrote Andrzej Wajda's film 'Innocent Sorcerers,' entering the Polish film industry as a screenwriter.
Co-wrote Roman Polański's 'Knife in the Water,' one of the most acclaimed Polish films of the era.
Directed feature debut 'Identification Marks: None' (Rysopis), winning awards at festivals in Arnhem and Warsaw.
Won the Golden Bear at the Berlin Film Festival for 'The Departure.'
Directed 'The Shout,' which won the Grand Jury Prize at Cannes.
Directed 'Moonlighting' starring Jeremy Irons, a critical success about martial law in Poland.
Directed 'Essential Killing,' starring Vincent Gallo, winning the Special Jury Prize at Venice.
Directed 'EO,' which won the Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival and was nominated for Best International Film at the Oscars.

name: Zoran Primorac
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship silver in men's doubles at the 1987 World Championships in New Delhi at age 18, followed by Olympic silver at the 1988 Seoul Olympics and European Championship gold in 1990, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Zadar, Croatia (then Yugoslavia), Primorac started playing table tennis at his hometown club STK Bagat. His father's workplace connection to coach Tomislav Amižić provided early expert coaching. He won seven medals at European Youth Championships, moved to Zagreb club Vjesnik in 1985, and broke through internationally with World Championship silver in 1987 alongside doubles partner Ilija Lupulesku.
family_context_summary: Born in Zadar, Yugoslavia (now Croatia); father worked for the same company as table tennis coach Tomislav Amižić, which provided the connection to expert early coaching.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's workplace connection to coach Tomislav Amižić provided early access to expert table tennis coaching; no direct family table tennis background documented.
evidence_summary: Zoran Primorac was born in Zadar, Croatia (then Yugoslavia) and began playing table tennis at his hometown club STK Bagat. His father's workplace connection to coach Tomislav Amižić provided early expert coaching, with Amižić's son Mario later taking over as his coach. As a junior, Primorac won seven medals at European Youth Championships. At age 18, he won World Championship silver in doubles with partner Ilija Lupulesku, followed by Olympic silver in 1988 and European Championship gold in 1990, all before age 26. The durable doubles partnership with Lupulesku was a key multiplier.
starting_point: Born in 1969 in Zadar, SR Croatia (Yugoslavia); father's workplace connection to a table tennis coach provided early access to expert coaching at hometown club STK Bagat.
current_position: Retired from competitive table tennis; one of only three table tennis players to compete at seven Olympic Games (1988-2012); highest ITTF world ranking was number 2 in 1998.

trajectory.event: Won World Championship silver medal in men's doubles with Ilija Lupulesku at the New Delhi World Championships.
Won Olympic silver medal in men's doubles at the Seoul Olympics with Lupulesku.
Won European Championship gold in men's doubles in Gothenburg with Lupulesku.
Won bronze medal in men's singles at the World Table Tennis Championships.
Achieved career-high ITTF world ranking of number 2.
Competed in his seventh Olympic Games in London, becoming one of only three table tennis players to do so.

name: Careca
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Brazilian Championship (Série A) with Guarani in his first professional season in 1978 at age 18, and by age 26 led São Paulo to the 1986 Brazilian Championship while winning the Bola de Ouro as Brazilian Footballer of the Year.
early_history_summary: Born in Araraquara, São Paulo state, Careca began his professional career with Guarani in 1978, immediately winning the Brazilian Championship in his first season. He moved to São Paulo in 1983 and became one of Brazil's most prolific strikers, leading São Paulo to the 1986 Brazilian Championship and earning the Bola de Ouro award.
family_context_summary: Born in Araraquara, São Paulo state, Brazil; family background not extensively documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Careca was born in Araraquara, Brazil in 1960 and began his professional football career with Guarani in 1978 at age 18, immediately winning the Brazilian Championship in his first season. His prolific finishing and pace quickly established him as one of Brazil's best young strikers. He moved to São Paulo in 1983 and by 1986 led the club to another Brazilian Championship while winning the Bola de Ouro as the country's Footballer of the Year, all before age 26. Family background details are not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in 1960 in Araraquara, São Paulo state, Brazil; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired former professional footballer; last known residing in Brazil; career included 64 caps for Brazil national team (1982-1993) and notable spells at Napoli alongside Diego Maradona.

trajectory.event: Began professional career with Guarani and won the Brazilian Championship (Série A) in his first season.
Signed by São Paulo FC, continuing as one of Brazil's most prolific strikers.
Led São Paulo to the Brazilian Championship and won the Bola de Ouro as Brazilian Footballer of the Year.
Transferred to Napoli in Italy, joining Diego Maradona to form one of Europe's most formidable attacking partnerships.
Helped Napoli win the Serie A title and the UEFA Cup, scoring crucial goals.
Represented Brazil at the 1990 FIFA World Cup in Italy.

name: Tomohiko Ikoma
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Emperor's Cup in 1953 (age 21) and 1955 (age 23) with All Kwangaku, and debuted for the Japan national team on January 2, 1955, earning 5 caps for Japan, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Hyogo Prefecture, Ikoma played football at Kobe High School and then Kwansei Gakuin University, where he was part of the All Kwangaku team that won two Emperor's Cup titles. He joined Mitsubishi Motors after graduation and later became a playing manager, representing Japan internationally in 1955.
family_context_summary: Born in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan in 1932; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Tomohiko Ikoma was born in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan in 1932. He played at Kobe High School and then Kwansei Gakuin University, where as part of the All Kwangaku team he won the Emperor's Cup in 1953 and 1955, Japan's most prestigious football competition. He debuted for the Japan national team on January 2, 1955 against Burma, earning 5 caps that year. After graduation he joined Mitsubishi Motors as a player and later became playing manager. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in 1932 in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on April 27, 2009 at age 76 in Kobe, Hyogo, Japan; final role was as playing manager of Mitsubishi Motors in 1966 before retiring from football.

trajectory.event: Won the Emperor's Cup with All Kwangaku (Kwansei Gakuin University team), Japan's most prestigious football competition.
Won the Emperor's Cup again with All Kwangaku and debuted for the Japan national team against Burma on January 2, earning 5 caps.
Joined Mitsubishi Motors as a professional player after graduating from university.
Participated in the inaugural season of the Japan Soccer League with Mitsubishi Motors.
Became playing manager of Mitsubishi Motors for one season before retiring from football.
Died on April 27, 2009 in Kobe, Hyogo, Japan.

name: Gary Oldman
milestone_by_age_26: Made professional film debut in 'Remembrance' (1982) at age 24 and was performing at major theaters including the Glasgow Citizens Theatre and the Royal Court Theatre, establishing a professional acting career before 26.
early_history_summary: Raised in a working-class family in south London by a single mother after his alcoholic father left when he was 7, Oldman dropped out of school at 16 but discovered acting through the Greenwich Young People's Theatre. He earned a scholarship to Rose Bruford College, graduating in 1979, and quickly found professional theater work before making his film debut in 1982.
family_context_summary: Son of a welder/former sailor father who was an alcoholic and left the family when Oldman was 7, and a homemaker mother; raised in a working-class neighborhood in south London (New Cross).
parent_family_domain_summary: No family connections to acting or the arts; father was a welder and former sailor, mother was a homemaker. Older sister Maureen (Laila Morse) later became an actress.
evidence_summary: Gary Oldman was born in 1958 in New Cross, London to a working-class family; his father, an alcoholic welder and former sailor, left when Oldman was 7. He dropped out of school at 16 but discovered acting through the Greenwich Young People's Theatre, then earned a scholarship to Rose Bruford College, graduating in 1979. He was the first in his year to receive professional work, performing at York Theatre Royal, Glasgow Citizens Theatre, and eventually the Royal Court Theatre and Royal Shakespeare Company. His film debut in 'Remembrance' (1982) at age 24 marked his entry into professional cinema, with his breakthrough coming at 28 with 'Sid and Nancy' (1986).
starting_point: Born in 1958 in New Cross, London to a working-class family; father was a welder and former sailor who left when Oldman was 7; raised by his homemaker mother in south London.
current_position: Academy Award-winning actor; won Oscar for Best Actor for 'Darkest Hour' (2017); active in film and television, recently known for 'Slow Horses' (Apple TV+); estimated net worth approximately $40 million.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Rose Bruford College with a BA in Acting and began professional theater work at York Theatre Royal.
Made professional film debut in 'Remembrance,' directed by Colin Gregg.
Won Drama Magazine Award and Fringe Award for best newcomer for 'The Pope's Wedding' at the Royal Court Theatre.
Rose to prominence portraying Sid Vicious in 'Sid and Nancy,' winning the Evening Standard Award for best newcomer in a film.
Achieved international recognition as Count Dracula in Francis Ford Coppola's 'Bram Stoker's Dracula.'
Earned his first Academy Award nomination for 'Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy.'
Won the Academy Award for Best Actor for portraying Winston Churchill in 'Darkest Hour.'

name: Ali Shariati
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the Islamic Students' Association in 1952 at age 19 and became a high school teacher, establishing himself as a political activist and intellectual; by age 26 he had earned his bachelor's degree and begun doctoral studies at the University of Paris.
early_history_summary: Born in northeastern Persia to a family of clerics, Shariati's father was an Islamic scholar who established the Centre for the Propagation of Islamic Truth. Shariati was exposed to Western philosophy and political thought at the Teacher's Training College in Mashhad, wrote for the Khorasan daily newspaper, and founded the Islamic Students' Association at 19. He earned his bachelor's degree in 1955 and won a scholarship to the University of Paris by 1959.
family_context_summary: Born to a family of clerics in Mazinan, Sabzevar; father Mohammad-Taqi was a teacher and Islamic scholar who established the Centre for the Propagation of Islamic Truth in Mashhad. Mother came from a small land-owning family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an Islamic scholar and teacher who founded a social Islamic forum involved in political movements, directly transferring religious and political knowledge to Shariati from childhood.
evidence_summary: Ali Shariati was born in 1933 in northeastern Persia to a family of clerics. His father, Mohammad-Taqi, was an Islamic scholar who established the Centre for the Propagation of Islamic Truth in Mashhad, immersing Shariati in religious and political discourse from childhood. At the Teacher's Training College, he encountered Western philosophy and began writing for the Khorasan newspaper. At 19, he founded the Islamic Students' Association and was arrested following a demonstration. He earned his bachelor's degree in 1955 and by 1959 had won a scholarship to the University of Paris, where he engaged with Frantz Fanon, Jean-Paul Sartre, and the Algerian FLN, all before age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1933 in Mazinan, Sabzevar, Persia to a family of clerics; father was an Islamic scholar and teacher who founded the Centre for the Propagation of Islamic Truth in Mashhad.
current_position: Died on June 18, 1977 at age 43 in Southampton, England under mysterious circumstances (believed killed by SAVAK); buried in Damascus next to Sayyidah Zaynab; his writings became foundational to the Iranian Revolution.

trajectory.event: Founded the Islamic Students' Association and became a high school teacher, leading to his first arrest following a demonstration.
Received his bachelor's degree from the University of Mashhad.
Won a scholarship to the University of Paris and began collaborating with the Algerian National Liberation Front (FLN).
Co-founded the Freedom Movement of Iran abroad with Ebrahim Yazdi, Mostafa Chamran, and Sadegh Qotbzadeh.
Earned PhD in Persian language from the University of Paris and returned to Iran, where he was arrested and imprisoned.
Began lecturing at the Hosseiniye Ershad Institute in Tehran, attracting massive popular following.
Released from eighteen months in solitary confinement after widespread public pressure and international outcry.
Died on June 18, 1977 in Southampton, England under mysterious circumstances, believed killed by SAVAK.

name: Otoya Yamaguchi
milestone_by_age_26: Assassinated Inejirō Asanuma, chairman of the Japan Socialist Party, on October 12, 1960 at age 17, an act captured in a Pulitzer Prize-winning photograph; died by suicide in detention on November 2, 1960.
early_history_summary: Born in Tokyo to a military officer father and the granddaughter of a famous writer, Yamaguchi exhibited intense xenophobia and nationalist sentiments from childhood. He dropped out of high school to join right-wing extremist activities, formally joining Bin Akao's Greater Japan Patriotic Party at age 16 before carrying out the assassination of Asanuma at 17.
family_context_summary: Son of Shinpei Yamaguchi, a high-ranking officer in the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, and maternal grandson of famous writer Namiroku Murakami, known for novels glorifying yakuza culture.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a military officer (Japan Ground Self-Defense Force) and maternal grandfather was a famous writer of violent novels about yakuza, providing a culturally nationalist household environment.
evidence_summary: Otoya Yamaguchi was born in 1943 in Tokyo to a military officer father (who became a high-ranking Japan Ground Self-Defense Force officer) and a mother who was the granddaughter of famous writer Namiroku Murakumi. He exhibited intense xenophobia and nationalist sentiments from childhood, clashing with teachers and dropping out of high school. At 16, he joined Bin Akao's far-right Greater Japan Patriotic Party after hearing a speech by Akao. At 17, he assassinated Japan Socialist Party chairman Inejirō Asanuma on live television, then committed suicide in detention. The assassination photograph won the Pulitzer Prize and World Press Photo of the Year.
starting_point: Born in 1943 in Yanaka, Taitō ward, Tokyo; father was a military officer (later high-ranking in Japan Ground Self-Defense Force), maternal grandfather was famous writer Namiroku Murakami.
current_position: Died on November 2, 1960 at age 17 in Nerima, Tokyo by suicide by hanging while in detention; known for the assassination of Inejirō Asanuma, chairman of the Japan Socialist Party.

trajectory.event: Joined Bin Akao's far-right Greater Japan Patriotic Party after hearing a speech declaring Japan was on the verge of revolution.
Assassinated Japan Socialist Party chairman Inejirō Asanuma with a wakizashi short sword during a televised election debate on October 12, 1960.
Committed suicide by hanging in a detention facility on November 2, 1960, while awaiting prosecution.
